```
Administrative commands for managing runners and registration tokens.

These commands require admin privileges.

Usage:
  spin admin [flags]
  spin admin [command]

Available Commands:
  logs        Search what the installation's processes logged
  runner      Manage registered runners
  storage     What the object store holds, and taking out what nothing needs
  token       Manage runner registration tokens
  versions    What is running where: this control plane, each runner and its machine

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for admin

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")

Use "spin admin [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

### spin admin logs

```
Search what the control plane, the proxy and the runners logged, newest first.

The query is Quickwit's query language; empty is everything in the window.

Examples:
  spin admin logs
  spin admin logs 'severity_text:error' --since 24h
  spin admin logs 'service_name:runner AND body.message:"no host"' --limit 20

Usage:
  spin admin logs [query] [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help             help for logs
      --limit int32      how many records, newest first: 1 to 1000 (default 100)
      --since duration   how far back to look, at most 744h (31 days) (default 1h0m0s)

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin runner activate

```
Let a drained or cordoned runner take new workspaces again.

A revoked runner is not brought back by this: its machine cannot connect again.

Usage:
  spin admin runner activate <runner-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for activate

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin runner drain

```
Stop a runner taking new workspaces, until it is activated (spin admin runner activate).

Existing workspaces continue to run until stopped.

With --suspend, every running workspace is suspended off the runner: its memory
and disk go to the object store, and its next start resumes it, on this runner
or another. The command returns once each is suspended or has failed to be.

Usage:
  spin admin runner drain <runner-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help      help for drain
      --suspend   Suspend the runner's running workspaces so they resume elsewhere

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin runner policy

```
Show or set what this installation decides about one runner.

A runner reads what it *is* - where the control plane is, who to trust, where it keeps its
data - from its own environment, before it can reach anything. Everything else it is told
here, on its heartbeat, and it reports back the revision it is running under: "declared" and
"running" being different for more than a moment is a runner that did not take it.

With no flags this shows the policy. Any flag writes it, and a write is the whole policy:
what you do not pass is the installation saying nothing about that setting, which leaves the
runner on its own default.

Usage:
  spin admin runner policy <runner-id> [flags]

Flags:
      --boot-from-template               restore workspaces on this runner from one frozen machine instead of booting each; every machine there then shares one kernel memory layout (KASLR)
      --cpu-cores int32                  cores this runner advertises; unset advertises what it has
      --disk-gb int32                    disk this runner advertises; unset advertises what it has
  -h, --help                             help for policy
      --max-workspace-cpu-cores int32    the cores one workspace may grow to there
      --max-workspace-memory-mb int32    the memory one workspace may grow to there
      --memory-mb int32                  memory this runner advertises; unset advertises what it has
      --preemptible                      a stop on this runner is the machine being taken away, not a restart
      --preemption-metadata-url string   where that cloud's metadata service answers; empty is its own link-local address
      --preemption-source string         the cloud that announces a reclaim: aws, gcp or azure (implies --preemptible)
      --shutdown-grace duration          how long this runner stays up after a stop signal so its workspaces can be moved off it

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin runner revoke

```
Revoke a runner's access to the platform: for a machine being replaced, or one that may
be compromised.

The runner is disconnected and its credentials deleted: that machine cannot come back, and
the capacity returns only with a new machine. To stop a runner taking new workspaces for a
while, drain it instead (spin admin runner drain).

A runner that holds workspaces' disks is refused, naming them: each could then run only once
recovered onto another runner (spin workspace recover), losing what this one had not published.
--leave-workspaces revokes it anyway.

Usage:
  spin admin runner revoke <runner-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help               help for revoke
      --leave-workspaces   revoke although workspaces are on this host; each runs again only once recovered elsewhere
  -y, --yes                Skip confirmation

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin storage remove

```
Remove an image, an extension release, an unclaimed volume or an orphan from the store:
its row, then its volume, whose key is destroyed. Its layers go at storage-gc's next run.

An image its ref still offers is retired first (spin admin storage retire-image); the newest
release of an extension, one a workspace runs, and a workspace's disk are refused.

Usage:
  spin admin storage remove <volume-id> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for remove
  -y, --yes    Skip confirmation

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin storage retire-image

```
Stop offering an image to new workspaces. The disks already cloned from it go on reading
it; once none does, it can be removed (spin admin storage remove).

Usage:
  spin admin storage retire-image <ref> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for retire-image

Global Flags:

      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```

#### spin admin token create

```
Create a token for registering a new runner: one-time, or with --reusable a pool's.

The token will be displayed only once. Save it securely.

A pool's token registers every machine that presents it until it expires or is revoked: what
an autoscaling group's machines take, with nobody at them. Keep it short-lived and rotate it
(the control plane's own machine can mint one with `controlplane registration-token`).

The policy flags are what every runner the token registers starts with, as `spin admin runner
policy` would set them: a spot group's runners need to know from their first heartbeat that
a stop is a reclaim. A runner registering again keeps what was decided about it since.

Examples:
  spin admin token create --description "Host us-east-1"
  spin admin token create --description "Team runner" --team engineering
  spin admin token create --description "Temp runner" --expires 1h
  spin admin token create --description "spot group" --reusable --expires 168h \
    --preemption-source aws --shutdown-grace 100s

Usage:
  spin admin token create [flags]

Flags:
      --boot-from-template               restore workspaces on each host it registers from one frozen machine instead of booting each; every machine there then shares one kernel memory layout (KASLR)
      --cpu-cores int32                  cores each host it registers advertises; unset advertises what it has
      --description string               Description for the token
      --disk-gb int32                    disk each host it registers advertises; unset advertises what it has
      --expires duration                 how long the token registers hosts; unset is the control plane's 24 hours, and at most 30 days
  -h, --help                             help for create
      --max-workspace-cpu-cores int32    the cores one workspace may grow to there
      --max-workspace-memory-mb int32    the memory one workspace may grow to there
      --memory-mb int32                  memory each host it registers advertises; unset advertises what it has
      --preemptible                      a stop on each host it registers is the machine being taken away, not a restart
      --preemption-metadata-url string   where that cloud's metadata service answers; empty is its own link-local address
      --preemption-source string         the cloud that announces a reclaim: aws, gcp or azure (implies --preemptible)
      --reusable                         a pool's token: it registers every host that presents it until it expires
      --shutdown-grace duration          how long each host it registers stays up after a stop signal so its workspaces can be moved off it
      --team string                      Team ID to scope the runner to

Global Flags:
      --config string    config file (default is $HOME/.spin/config.yaml)
  -o, --output string    text for a person, or json: one document of what the API answered, and no prose (default "text")
      --profile string   named profile to use (default "default")
```
